为什么每天花五分钟复盘: Why spend five minutes a day reviewing
比记住更重要的，是看见自己: More important than remembering is seeing yourself
我们每天都在做很多事，但大部分在睡前就已经模糊了。复盘不是写总结报告，而是在一天: We do so much every day, yet most of it blurs by bedtime. Reviewing isn’t writing a report; it’s pausing at the end of the day to look at who you were today.
五分钟就够。你不需要写得很好，只需要写得真实。“今天只背了 10 个单词”也是一: Five minutes is enough. You don’t need to write well, just honestly. “Only learned 10 words today” is a valuable record too, because it shows you your real pace.
坚持一段时间后，你会发现这些零散的句子会慢慢连成一条线。你能看出自己在什么时候状: After a while, these scattered lines slowly join into a thread. You’ll see when you’re at your best, what you keep putting off, and which little things make you happy.
复盘真正的价值，不在于某一天写了什么，而在于你开始认识自己。: The real value of reviewing isn’t what you wrote on any one day; it’s that you start to know yourself.
三个问题，做好一次复盘: Three questions for a good review
做了什么、学到什么、明天怎么做: What I did, what I learned, what I’ll do tomorrow
如果不知道写什么，可以试试这三个问题。: If you don’t know what to write, try these three questions.
第一，今天做了什么？只写事实，不评价。比如“读了 20 页书”“整理了书桌”。事: First, what did I do today? Just facts, no judgment, like “read 20 pages” or “tidied my desk”. Facts free you from the feeling that “I didn’t do anything today”.
第二，学到了什么？可以是一个知识点，也可以是对自己的一个发现。比如“下午三点以后: Second, what did I learn? A piece of knowledge, or something about yourself, like “I can hardly focus after 3 pm”.
第三，明天怎么做？只写一件小事就好。比如“明天把最难的任务放在上午”。: Third, what will I do tomorrow? Just one small thing, like “do the hardest task in the morning”.
三个问题，三句话，一次完整的复盘就完成了。: Three questions, three sentences, and a full review is done.
没做到的日子，也值得记录: Days you missed are worth recording too
很多人放弃记录，是从某一天没做到开始的。空着的那一天像一个污点，让人不想再打开。: Many people give up recording after a day they missed. That blank day feels like a stain, and they stop opening the app.
但复盘不是考勤，它只是一面镜子。没做到的那天，写一句“今天太累了，先休息”，这本: But reviewing isn’t attendance; it’s just a mirror. On a missed day, writing “Too tired today, resting first” is an honest review in itself.
节奏会有起伏，这很正常。重要的不是每一天都完美，而是你愿意回来。: Your rhythm will rise and fall, and that’s normal. What matters isn’t being perfect every day, but being willing to come back.
所以我们没有在卡片上显示“连续几天”。你随时可以停下，也随时可以重新开始。: That’s why we don’t show streaks on cards. You can stop anytime, and start again anytime.
习惯越少，越容易坚持: Fewer habits are easier to keep
先从两三件小事开始: Start with two or three small things
刚开始复盘时，很多人会一口气加上七八张卡片，结果没几天就觉得累。: When starting out, many people add seven or eight cards at once and feel tired within days.
更好的方式是从两三件最在意的小事开始。等它们变成自然而然的事，再慢慢加新的。: A better way is to start with the two or three small things you care about most. Once they feel natural, add new ones slowly.
如果某张卡片连续很久都没点亮，不用自责。它也许只是不适合现在的你，删掉或者换一种: If a card hasn’t lit up for a long time, don’t blame yourself. Maybe it just doesn’t fit you right now; delete it or rephrase it.
卡片少一点，每一次点亮就更有分量。: With fewer cards, each one you light up means more.
周末十分钟，做一次周复盘: Ten minutes on the weekend for a weekly review
从每天的点，连成每周的线: From daily dots to a weekly line
小满记录的是细节，周复盘看的是方向。: Xiaoman records the details; a weekly review shows the direction.
周末找十分钟，打开“总结”页，看看这一周：哪张卡片最常出现？哪张几乎没有动过？写: Find ten minutes on the weekend, open the “Summary” page and look at the week: which card shows up most? Which barely moved? Any feelings or problems that keep coming up in what you wrote?
然后只做一个决定：下周想调整什么？可能是减少一张卡片，也可能是把某件事换个时间做: Then make just one decision: what do I want to adjust next week? Maybe drop a card, or move something to a different time.
好的复盘会让事情变得更轻，而不是更重。如果你觉得累了，删掉一张卡片，也是一次很好: A good review makes things lighter, not heavier. If you feel tired, deleting a card is a good adjustment too.
